# Financial Time Series

## Definition
A **financial time series** is a sequence of numerical data points representing financial variables measured or recorded at successive points in time, typically at uniform intervals.

---

## Common Examples

| Time Series | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| **Stock prices** | Daily closing prices of a stock |
| **Exchange rates** | USD/EUR rate over time |
| **Interest rates** | Federal funds rate history |
| **Trading volume** | Shares traded per day |
| **Volatility** | Price fluctuation measures |
| **Index values** | S&P 500, NASDAQ levels |

---

## Key Characteristics

- **Non-stationarity** – Mean and variance often change over time
- **Volatility clustering** – Large changes tend to follow large changes
- **Fat tails** – Extreme events occur more than normal distribution suggests
- **Serial correlation** – Past values may influence future values
- **Seasonality** – Patterns repeating at regular intervals
- **Noise** – High degree of randomness

---

## Why It Matters

- **Forecasting** prices or returns
- **Risk management** (VaR, portfolio risk)
- **Algorithmic trading** strategies
- **Economic analysis** and policy decisions

---

## Common Analytical Methods

- ARIMA models
- GARCH (volatility modeling)
- Machine learning (LSTM, etc.)
- Technical analysis
